question: What discoveries have been made regarding the topological charge corresponding to bound states in the continuum?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer states the central discovery: BICs in periodic dielectric slabs are vortex centers of the far-field polarization field, with the topological charge defined as the integer winding number of the polarization vectors around the vortex center.
examples: BICs are vortex centers in the polarization direction of far-field radiation; the charge is the number of times polarization vectors wind around the vortex center
Each BIC appears as a topological defect (vortex) in the polarization long axes with an integer topological charge of ±1

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer states that both symmetry-protected and accidental (robust, non-symmetry-protected) BICs in photonic crystal slabs carry such topological charges.
examples: Both types of BICs in a periodic dielectric slab are vortex centers of the far-field polarization
Symmetry-protected BICs and accidental BICs in photonic crystal slabs both correspond to polarization vortices with quantized charges

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains that the robustness of previously 'accidental' BICs arises from these conserved, quantized charges, which can only be changed through large parameter variations.
examples: The robustness of these BICs is due to conserved and quantized topological charges
Charges are conserved and can only be generated or annihilated by making large changes in system parameters

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that symmetries constrain the charges and that their generation, evolution, and annihilation obey strict rules (e.g., annihilation only when opposite charges meet), derived and tested numerically.
examples: Charges are generated or annihilated only by large parameter changes and only according to strict rules
The symmetries constraining the charges and their generation, evolution, and annihilation were derived

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer describes the discovery that tuning a parameter (e.g., lattice periodicity) moves off-center BIC charges through momentum space toward the Brillouin zone center, where multiple charges merge into a single BIC (charge +1) with total charge conserved.
examples: When a increases from 519.25 nm to 531.42 nm, eight off-center BICs move to the center and merge with the symmetry-pinned one into a single BIC of charge +1
The merged BIC persists when a further increases to 580 nm

ingredients.name: answer_critical_5
ingredients.criterion: The answer connects merged-charge BICs to on-chip resonances with suppressed out-of-plane scattering loss and ultrahigh quality factors (Q diverges at the BIC).
examples: Merging multiple BICs yields ultrahigh-Q resonances robust to out-of-plane scattering losses
At the BIC the quality factor diverges to infinity

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that only symmetry-pinned charges (e.g., at the Brillouin zone center) are fixed, while the locations of other charges can be controlled by system parameters such as periodicity.
examples: One vortex is pinned at the Brillouin zone center by symmetry; the other eight move with periodicity
Charge positions in momentum space are tunable via structure parameters

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer situates the discovery within wider physics, such as Berry phases around Dirac points, topological defects, and vortex physics, or conjectures that robust BICs generally correspond to topological defects in parameter space.
examples: The finding connects electromagnetic BICs to Berry phases around Dirac points and general vortex physics
It is conjectured that most robust BICs correspond to topological defects in appropriate parameter spaces

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer cites applications flowing from these discoveries, such as lasing at BIC states, vector beam generation, and on-chip beam steering.
examples: Lasing can naturally occur at BIC states where Q diverges; emission generates vector beams useful for optical trapping and STED microscopy
Angular (wave-vector) tunability of BICs makes them candidates for on-chip beam steering
